review.reviewBody: I used to spend hours every week ordering food. Now it's simple, super easy, and I have free time to spend on other aspects of my restaurant.

@graph.name: From a guide export to the first spoken reorder
@graph.description: Your team sends the products each restaurant buys from you. We build the accounts, and every chef puts our app on their phone.

step.name: Export each account's regular items
step.text: A spreadsheet from your ERP or from RepZio is usually all we need, listing every account's regular products and prices.

step.name: Restaurant accounts go live
step.text: We load the restaurant's guide into our admin and open its account. For most restaurants, the first order comes the same day.

step.name: Reorders arrive just as the chef sent them
step.text: Each order from the app has its own number and the time it was sent. A reorder still phoned to a rep gets no number from us.

@graph.name: Do I need a RepZio alternative for spoken reorders?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. RepZio stays in your reps' hands for presentations, showroom selling and the storefront. What changes is the reorder a chef phones or messages to the rep today: now it is spoken in our app, checked by the chef and sent.

@graph.name: Is VoiceOrder Solutions better than RepZio?

acceptedAnswer.text: At one job: letting a chef send the usual restaurant order unaided, spoken and then looked over, with no rep in between. Winning the account, showing new products and selling at trade events are RepZio's work, so we stay alongside it and are not a RepZio alternative.

@graph.name: A rep just sold a restaurant something new. How does it get on their list?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your team adds it to the guide for that restaurant in our admin. Once it is there, the chef can say it along with the rest of the reorder and see it listed before sending. The rep still makes the sale in RepZio, as now; our app only handles what the kitchen orders again.

@graph.name: Is it linked to RepZio, and does my desk end up typing these reorders?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are not linked. RepZio and VoiceOrder Solutions are made by separate firms with no connection between them, and each one supports only its own product. Your ERP keeps your accounts, stock and billing, and RepZio keeps the orders your reps write; we hold every restaurant's guide with its prices, plus the reorders sent through our app. By email, your desk gets a file of the approved items and keys it in from that. What it saves is the call itself: nobody answers the phone, notes every item and repeats the list back, because the chef reviewed the order before it was sent. Sent by EDI or API, it can land in your ERP untouched by your desk, provided your ERP is configured for it, and the demo is where we find out.

@graph.name: Will our reps lose sight of their accounts?

acceptedAnswer.text: They need not. Emailed orders can be sent to a rep, and whether each account's orders can reach its own rep, as well as the desk, is something to confirm in the demo. App orders will not appear in the rep's RepZio order list, since they do not go through RepZio.

@graph.name: RepZio works offline. Does your app?

acceptedAnswer.text: RepZio's rep app can write orders without a signal, which matters on a show floor or out in a territory. We can't promise that for our app, so ask about it in the demo. What it does do is save an order if the chef gets pulled away, so they can pick up where they stopped.

@graph.name: How quickly can we start, and what will it cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Setup takes 24 to 48 hours for most distributors, and RepZio is left exactly as it is. You pass us the products each account normally orders, often exported to a spreadsheet; we put them into our admin, create every account, and the restaurants download our app, most of them ordering that same day. RepZio lists no prices on its site; its support site describes a free Basic rep license for browsing and a paid monthly Standard license for sending orders. We quote per distributor. A RepZio replacement would mean new tools for every rep before the next trade show; with us, every rep keeps the tools they have.

@graph.name: Where do the RepZio details on this page come from?

acceptedAnswer.text: We read repzio.com and the RepZio support site on 9 November 2026: the home, solutions, sales rep app, B2B Direct, ShopZio, integrations and price pages, and support guides for the iOS app, the web app and market prep. The example of a rep keying in an order taken by phone comes from a partner's blog post about RepZio. We searched for a voice tool sold for RepZio and came up empty.
